records.source: Εἰ οὖν συνηγέρθητε τῷ Χριστῷ, τὰ ἄνω ζητεῖτε, οὗ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ καθήμενος·
records.gloss: If then you were raised with the Christ, the things above seek, where the Christ is at [the] right [hand] of the God sitting;
pieces: You have been raised with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, then. So seek what is above, where {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} sits at the right hand of God.

L.1: If then you were raised with the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, seek the things above, where the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is, seated at the right [hand] of God.

R.1: God raised you to new life with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. So keep looking for the things of heaven, where {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is. He is sitting in the place of honor at God's right side.

decisions.choice: if then: since, a fact already true of them
decisions.reason: Εἰ οὖν draws on what 2:12 said: they were raised with Christ in baptism. As in 2:20, "if" states something Paul takes as settled.

decisions.choice: the things above: the realm where Christ reigns, and all that belongs to it
alternatives: heavenly visions and experiences (as the teachers offered, 2:18)
decisions.reason: "Above" is not a place to escape to but the realm where Christ is, defined at once: "where Christ is". Verse 2 sets it against "the things on the earth", and verses 5-17 show what seeking it looks like in everyday life.

decisions.choice: seated at the right hand of God: Psalm 110:1
decisions.reason: God says to the king, "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool" (Psalm 110:1). The right hand is the place of honor and authority, and the psalm is often applied to the risen Jesus (Acts 2:34-35). From there he rules over the powers (2:10, 2:15).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: God raised you to new life; the place of honor at God's right side
alternatives: you were raised; at the right hand of God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raised them (2:12) and says what the right hand stands for (m3).

records.heading: Raised with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}

records.source: τὰ ἄνω φρονεῖτε, μὴ τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἀπεθάνετε γάρ, καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν κέκρυπται σὺν τῷ Χριστῷ ἐν τῷ θεῷ·
records.gloss: the things above set [your] mind on, not the things on the earth, \v 3 you died for, and the life of you has been hidden with the Christ in the God;
pieces: Fix your thoughts on what is above, not on what is on earth.
For you died, and the life you now have lies hidden with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in God.

L.2: Set [your] mind on the things above, not on the things on the earth,
L.3: for you died, and your life has been hidden with the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} in God.

R.2: Think about the things of heaven, not the things of this earth.
R.3: Your old life has died. Your new life is kept safe with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in God, where no one can see it yet.

decisions.choice: set your mind on: give your thinking and your will to
decisions.reason: φρονέω is more than thinking about something: it is a settled way of thinking that steers what one wants and does (Philippians 2:5; Romans 8:5).

decisions.choice: the things on the earth: life ordered by what passes away
decisions.reason: Paul does not call the created world bad; the rules he has just rejected treated food and the body with suspicion (2:21-23). "The things on the earth" are what verses 5-9 go on to list: the desires and habits of the old life.

decisions.choice: your life is hidden with Christ in God: kept safe, and not yet seen
decisions.reason: κέκρυπται ("has been hidden") is a perfect: their life is now kept with Christ, where no one can take it, and where it cannot yet be seen. Verse 4 says when it will be: when Christ appears.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: Your old life has died; where no one can see it yet
decisions.reason: Readable says what died (m3 and 2:20) and what "hidden" means here.

records.source: ὅταν ὁ Χριστὸς φανερωθῇ, ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν, τότε καὶ ὑμεῖς σὺν αὐτῷ φανερωθήσεσθε ἐν δόξῃ.
records.gloss: When the Christ is revealed, the life of you, then also you with him will be revealed in glory.
pieces: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is your life. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is revealed, you too will be revealed with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in glory.

L.4: When the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, your life, is revealed, then you also will be revealed with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in glory.

R.4: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is your true life. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes back and everyone sees {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, you will be seen with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and you will share in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "your life"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "our life", which would include Paul. The SBLGNT reads "your", which matches "your life" in verse 3. The meaning is not changed.

decisions.choice: revealed: made visible, when Christ comes
decisions.reason: φανερόω means to make visible what was hidden. The life hidden with Christ (verse 3) will be seen when he appears at his coming (1 John 3:2).

decisions.choice: in glory: sharing Christ's glory
decisions.reason: They will appear with him, and so in his glory (Romans 8:17-18). This is "the hope of glory" of 1:27.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: when he comes back and everyone sees him
decisions.reason: Readable says when and how he is revealed (m2).

records.source: Νεκρώσατε οὖν τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, πορνείαν, ἀκαθαρσίαν, πάθος, ἐπιθυμίαν κακήν, καὶ τὴν πλεονεξίαν ἥτις ἐστὶν εἰδωλολατρία, δι’ ἃ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς ἀπειθείας·
records.gloss: Put to death therefore the members the [ones] on the earth: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, desire evil, and the greed which is idolatry, \v 6 because of which things is coming the wrath of the God upon the sons of the disobedience;
pieces: So put to death whatever in you belongs to the earth: sexual immorality, impurity, lustful passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry.
Because of these things the wrath of God is coming on those who disobey.

L.5: Put to death, therefore, the members that are on the earth: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry,
L.6: because of which the wrath of God is coming on the {{gender:children|sons}} of disobedience.

R.5: So kill off every part of you that belongs to this earth: sexual sin, every kind of impure act, lust, evil desires, and greed. Greed is really a way of worshiping idols.
R.6: God's anger is coming because of these things, against people who refuse to obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the members on the earth: the parts of you that serve these earthly desires
decisions.reason: μέλη means the parts of the body. The body's parts are what a person uses to sin or to serve God (Romans 6:13; compare Matthew 5:29-30), and the list that follows names what is to die: deeds and desires, not the body itself.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: any sex outside marriage
decisions.reason: πορνείαν is the general word for sexual sin. The next words widen it: ἀκαθαρσίαν is impurity of any kind, πάθος uncontrolled passion, and ἐπιθυμίαν κακήν desire for what is evil.

decisions.choice: greed is idolatry: wanting more puts possessions in God's place
decisions.reason: πλεονεξίαν is the craving to have more. Paul calls it idolatry because what a person craves above everything becomes their god (Matthew 6:24; Ephesians 5:5).

decisions.choice: the wrath of God: God's settled judgment against evil
decisions.reason: ὀργὴ is God's just opposition to evil, not loss of temper. It "is coming": the final judgment is sure, and is already at work (Romans 1:18).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "on the sons of disobedience"
alternatives: no such words: "the wrath of God is coming"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts do not have these words, and they may have been added from the matching verse, Ephesians 5:6. Most manuscripts have them. Without them the sentence ends "the wrath of God is coming".

decisions.choice: the sons of disobedience: people whose lives are marked by disobedience
decisions.reason: "Sons of" something is a Hebrew way of saying people characterized by it (compare "children of light", 1 Thessalonians 5:5). It includes men and women.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means people of either sex (m6); "sons" is the traditional form. Balanced and Readable say "those who disobey", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: kill off
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the force of the verb in plain words.

decisions.choice: people who refuse to obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m6) and names God as the one disobeyed.

records.heading: Put to death what belongs to the earth

records.source: ἐν οἷς καὶ ὑμεῖς περιεπατήσατέ ποτε ὅτε ἐζῆτε ἐν τούτοις·
records.gloss: among whom also you walked once, when you were living in these;
pieces: You too once lived among such people, when your life was given over to these things.

L.7: Among them you also once walked, when you were living in these [things].

R.7: You used to live like those people, back when these things filled your life.

decisions.choice: among whom: among the disobedient of verse 6
decisions.reason: οἷς can be masculine (people) or neuter (the sins); the source data takes it as masculine. If "on the sons of disobedience" belongs in verse 6, "among whom" is natural; without those words it must mean "in which". The end of the verse, ἐν τούτοις ("in these"), then names the sins.

decisions.choice: walked and lived: how they behaved, and what their life consisted of
decisions.reason: περιπατέω ("walk") is how they conducted themselves, as in 1:10 and 2:6; ἐζῆτε ("you were living") says these things were the stuff of their life.

decisions.choice: lived
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure for how one lives; Literal keeps it.

records.source: νυνὶ δὲ ἀπόθεσθε καὶ ὑμεῖς τὰ πάντα, ὀργήν, θυμόν, κακίαν, βλασφημίαν, αἰσχρολογίαν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν·
records.gloss: now but put off also you the all things: anger, rage, malice, slander, obscene talk out of the mouth of you;
pieces: But now put all these away, every one: anger, bursts of temper, malice, slander, and foul words from your mouths.

L.8: But now you also must put away all [these]: anger, rage, malice, slander, obscene talk out of your mouth.

R.8: But now you must stop all of these things too: being angry, losing your temper, wanting to hurt others, saying evil things about people, and using dirty words.

decisions.choice: put away: take off, like clothes
decisions.reason: ἀποτίθημι is used for taking off clothing (Acts 7:58). The picture continues: they have put off the old self (verse 9), put on the new (verse 10), and are to put on compassion and love (verses 12-14).

decisions.choice: anger, rage, malice: settled anger, outbursts of temper, and the wish to harm
decisions.reason: ὀργήν is anger that is held; θυμόν is anger that flares up; κακίαν is ill will, the wish to hurt others.

decisions.choice: slander and obscene talk: speech that wounds and speech that degrades
decisions.reason: βλασφημίαν can mean blasphemy against God, but in a list of wrongs done to one another it means insulting or slandering people. αἰσχρολογίαν is filthy or abusive language.

decisions.choice: being angry, losing your temper, wanting to hurt others, saying evil things about people, and using dirty words
alternatives: anger, rage, malice, slander, obscene talk
decisions.reason: Readable turns the list of nouns into plain actions (m2, m3).

records.source: μὴ ψεύδεσθε εἰς ἀλλήλους· ἀπεκδυσάμενοι τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον σὺν ταῖς πράξεσιν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι τὸν νέον τὸν ἀνακαινούμενον εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν κατ’ εἰκόνα τοῦ κτίσαντος αὐτόν, ὅπου οὐκ ἔνι Ἕλλην καὶ Ἰουδαῖος, περιτομὴ καὶ ἀκροβυστία, βάρβαρος, Σκύθης, δοῦλος, ἐλεύθερος, ἀλλὰ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν Χριστός.
records.gloss: Do not lie to one another, having put off the old man with the practices of him, \v 10 and having put on the new, the [one] being renewed unto knowledge according to [the] image of the [one] having created him, \v 11 where there is not Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, free, but the all and in all Christ.
pieces: Do not lie to one another. You have stripped off the old self and its ways
and have put on the new self, which is being made new, growing in knowledge, in the image of its Creator.

In this new humanity it no longer counts whether one is Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian or Scythian, slave or free. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is everything, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is in all.

L.9: Do not lie to one another, since you have put off the old self with its practices
L.10: and have put on the new [self], which is being renewed for knowledge according to [the] image of the one who created it,
L.11: where there is not Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, free, but {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [is] all and in all.

R.9: Do not lie to each other. You have taken off your old life and the things you used to do, like old clothes.
R.10: You have put on a new life, and God keeps making it new, so that you know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} better and become more like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the one who created this new life.
R.11: In this new life it does not matter if you are a Greek or a Jew, circumcised or not, a foreigner or a wild outsider, a slave or free. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is all that matters, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives in all of you.

decisions.choice: since you have put off and put on: the reason for the command
alternatives: further commands: put off ... and put on
decisions.reason: The two participles are in the past tense and most naturally give the reason why they must not lie: this has already happened to them, when they were baptized and "stripped off" the old life (2:11-12, the same verb). In Ephesians 4:22-24 the same pictures are given as things to do.

decisions.choice: the old self: the person you were apart from Christ
alternatives: a sinful part within a person
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπον means a human being. "The old" one is not a part of a person but the whole of the old way of being human, and "the new" is the life given in Christ (Romans 6:6; Ephesians 2:15).

decisions.choice: renewed in the image of the creator: Genesis 1:26-27
decisions.reason: God made humankind in his image (Genesis 1:27). The new self is being remade after that image, which is Christ himself (1:15), so believers become what humans were made to be.

decisions.choice: for knowledge: renewed so as to know God truly
decisions.reason: ἐπίγνωσιν is the word for real knowledge used in 1:9-10 and 2:2. True knowledge comes with the new life, not from the teachers' visions.

decisions.choice: the deepest divisions of that world
decisions.reason: Greek and Jew divided people by race and religion; circumcision marked the covenant people. A βάρβαρος was anyone who did not speak Greek; the Σκύθης lived north of the Black Sea, and Greek writers used them as the type of the uncivilized. Slave and free was the legal line through every household.

decisions.choice: where: in the new humanity
decisions.reason: ὅπου ("where") means in the new self, the new humanity. The differences still exist in daily life (3:18-4:1 speaks to slaves and masters), but they no longer decide anyone's standing before God or in the church (Galatians 3:28).

decisions.choice: Christ is all and in all: he is everything that counts, and he lives in all his people
decisions.reason: πᾶσιν can be masculine ("in all people") or neuter ("in all things"). After a list of kinds of people, it most naturally means that Christ lives in every one of them.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the old self; the new self
alternatives: the old man; the new man
decisions.reason: The word means a human being (m2); "self" says that without making it a man.

decisions.choice: In this new humanity it no longer counts
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "where" refers to (m6).

decisions.choice: like old clothes; a foreigner or a wild outsider
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the clothing picture and says what "barbarian" and "Scythian" meant (m5).

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it in "slave or free" lists: the verse names slave and free as one of the divisions of that world (m5).

records.source: Ἐνδύσασθε οὖν ὡς ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἅγιοι καὶ ἠγαπημένοι, σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ, χρηστότητα, ταπεινοφροσύνην, πραΰτητα, μακροθυμίαν, ἀνεχόμενοι ἀλλήλων καὶ χαριζόμενοι ἑαυτοῖς ἐάν τις πρός τινα ἔχῃ μομφήν· καθὼς καὶ ὁ κύριος ἐχαρίσατο ὑμῖν οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς·
records.gloss: Put on therefore, as chosen [ones] of the God, holy and having been loved, a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience, \v 13 bearing with one another and forgiving each other if anyone against anyone has a complaint; just as also the Lord forgave you, so also you;
pieces: You are God's chosen people, holy and loved by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So put on, like clothing, a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.
Be patient with one another's faults, and when someone has a grievance against another, forgive. The Lord has forgiven you freely; you must do the same.

L.12: Put on, therefore, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience,
L.13: bearing with one another and forgiving each other, if anyone has a complaint against another; just as the Lord forgave you, so you also [must forgive].

R.12: God chose you to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people. You are holy, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves you. So be kind and caring to others, as if you were putting on new clothes. Be humble, gentle and patient.
R.13: Put up with each other. If someone has done wrong to you, forgive them. Forgive others, because the Lord forgave you.

decisions.choice: chosen, holy and loved: Israel's titles, given to the church
decisions.reason: God chose Israel to be holy and loved them (Deuteronomy 7:6-8). Paul gives the same titles to Gentile believers, whom God has made his people.

decisions.choice: a heart of compassion: deep, felt mercy
decisions.reason: σπλάγχνα means the inner organs, thought of as the seat of feeling (Philippians 1:8; 2:1); with οἰκτιρμοῦ it means compassion felt to the core.

decisions.choice: humility: the virtue, not the self-humbling of 2:18, 2:23
decisions.reason: ταπεινοφροσύνην is the word used of the teachers' self-humbling in 2:18 and 2:23. Here it is true lowliness of mind, seen in Christ (Philippians 2:3, 2:8).

decisions.choice: forgiving: giving freely, as God forgave
decisions.reason: χαρίζομαι is the verb used in 2:13 for God's forgiveness, and is related to the word for grace. They are to forgive as they have been forgiven.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the Lord"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "Christ", and some "God". "The Lord" here means Christ, as throughout this chapter (compare Ephesians 4:32, "God in Christ forgave you").

decisions.choice: so also you: so you also must forgive
decisions.reason: The verb is left out and is understood from what goes before.

decisions.choice: [must forgive]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb to be understood (m6).

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable say first who they are, then what to put on
decisions.reason: The titles give the reason for the command; putting them first makes that clear.

decisions.choice: be kind and caring to others; Be humble, gentle and patient
alternatives: a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience
decisions.reason: Readable turns the list of qualities into plain instructions.

records.heading: Clothed in love

records.source: ἐπὶ πᾶσιν δὲ τούτοις τὴν ἀγάπην, ὅ ἐστιν σύνδεσμος τῆς τελειότητος.
records.gloss: Over all and these [things] the love, which is [the] bond of the completeness.
pieces: Over all of these put on love, which binds everything together and makes it complete.

L.14: And over all these [put on] love, which is [the] bond of completeness.

R.14: Most important of all, love each other. Love holds everything together and makes it complete.

decisions.choice: over all these: on top of them, like an outer garment
alternatives: above all: most important of all
decisions.reason: The verb "put on" carries over from verse 12. ἐπὶ can mean "over" or "above all"; with the clothing picture, love is the garment that goes over all the rest. It is also the most important (1 Corinthians 13:13).

decisions.choice: the bond of completeness: love ties everything together so that it is complete
alternatives: love is the sum of all virtues
decisions.reason: σύνδεσμος is the word used in 2:19 for the ligaments that hold a body together. Love holds the virtues, and the people who practice them, together, and brings them to completeness. τελειότης is from the same root as the "mature" of 1:28.

decisions.choice: [put on]
decisions.reason: The verb is understood from verse 12 (m1).

decisions.choice: Most important of all
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the sense of priority (m1) without the clothing picture, which it has already explained.

records.source: καὶ ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Χριστοῦ βραβευέτω ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν, εἰς ἣν καὶ ἐκλήθητε ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι· καὶ εὐχάριστοι γίνεσθε.
records.gloss: And the peace of the Christ let rule in the hearts of you, to which also you were called in one body; and thankful be.
pieces: Let the peace that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gives be the umpire in your hearts. You were called to this peace as members of one body. And be thankful.

L.15: And let the peace of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} rule in your hearts, to which you were also called in one body; and be thankful.

R.15: Let the peace that comes from {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} decide things in your hearts. God called you to live in peace as one body. And always be thankful.

decisions.choice: rule: act as umpire, decide
decisions.reason: βραβεύω means to act as the umpire who decides a contest (the related verb in 2:18 is "disqualify"). When they differ, Christ's peace is to make the call.

decisions.choice: the peace of Christ: the peace he gives, among them as well as within
decisions.reason: It is the peace Christ gives (John 14:27) and made by his cross (1:20). They were called to it "in one body", so it is peace with one another as well as peace of heart.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the peace of Christ"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "God", as in Philippians 4:7. The meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: be the umpire
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the umpire (m1).

decisions.choice: God called you to live in peace as one body
alternatives: to which you were called in one body
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who called them, as in 1:12-13.

records.source: ὁ λόγος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐνοικείτω ἐν ὑμῖν πλουσίως ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ· διδάσκοντες καὶ νουθετοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ψαλμοῖς, ὕμνοις, ᾠδαῖς πνευματικαῖς ἐν χάριτι, ᾄδοντες ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν τῷ θεῷ·
records.gloss: The word of the Christ let dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing yourselves in psalms, hymns, songs spiritual, in grace, singing in the hearts of you to the God;
pieces: Let the word of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} make its home among you richly, in all wisdom. Teach and warn one another with psalms, hymns and Spirit-given songs, and sing to God, thankful from the heart.

L.16: Let the word of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, [and] spiritual songs, singing with gratitude in your hearts to God.

R.16: Let the message of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} fill your lives and make you wise. Teach each other and help each other do right with psalms, hymns and other songs that God's Spirit gives. Sing to God with thankful hearts.

decisions.choice: the word of Christ: the message about him, which is also his own word
decisions.reason: λόγος τοῦ Χριστοῦ can mean the message about Christ (the gospel, 1:5) or what Christ says; the two are one. It is to "dwell" among them, the verb used for God's fullness in Christ (2:9) in a related form.

decisions.choice: in all wisdom goes with "dwell"
alternatives: in all wisdom goes with "teaching and admonishing"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot after σοφίᾳ, so the wisdom goes with the word dwelling among them. Without it, the words could begin the next clause: "teaching ... in all wisdom", as in 1:28.

decisions.choice: psalms, hymns and spiritual songs: every kind of song the church sings
decisions.reason: The three words overlap. Psalms may be those of the Old Testament, hymns songs of praise to God, and songs any other sung words; "spiritual" probably covers all three as given by the Spirit. Verses like 1:15-20 may give an idea of such songs.

decisions.choice: with gratitude
decisions.reason: χάριτι is the word for grace, but it can also mean thanks (it is the word in 2 Corinthians 9:15, "thanks be to God"). With "be thankful" in verse 15 and "giving thanks" in verse 17, gratitude is likely here. It could also mean singing by God's grace.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the word of Christ"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "God" or "the Lord". "Christ" fits the run of verses 15-17.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: make its home
decisions.reason: "Dwell" says the same in older English; Balanced uses everyday words.

decisions.choice: make you wise; help each other do right
decisions.reason: Readable turns "in all wisdom" and "admonishing" into plain words.

records.source: καὶ πᾶν ὅ τι ἐὰν ποιῆτε ἐν λόγῳ ἢ ἐν ἔργῳ, πάντα ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, εὐχαριστοῦντες τῷ θεῷ πατρὶ δι’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And everything whatever you do in word or in deed, all [things] in [the] name of [the] Lord Jesus, giving thanks to the God Father through him.
pieces: In everything you say and everything you do, act in the name of the Lord Jesus, and through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} give thanks to God the Father.

L.17: And whatever you do, in word or in deed, [do] everything in [the] name of [the] Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God [the] Father through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.17: Whatever you say and whatever you do, do it as people who belong to the Lord Jesus. And through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} always thank God the Father.

decisions.choice: in the name of the Lord Jesus: as his people, under his authority
decisions.reason: To act "in the name" of someone is to act as one who belongs to them and represents them. Every word and deed is to be one Jesus can own.

decisions.choice: all: do everything
decisions.reason: The verb is left to be understood.

decisions.choice: through him: Jesus is the one through whom thanks reaches God
decisions.reason: Thanks is given to God the Father, and given through Jesus, by whom they have come to God (1:12-14).

decisions.choice: [do]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb to be understood (m2).

decisions.choice: as people who belong to the Lord Jesus
alternatives: in the name of the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1).

records.source: Αἱ γυναῖκες, ὑποτάσσεσθε τοῖς ἀνδράσιν, ὡς ἀνῆκεν ἐν κυρίῳ.
records.gloss: The wives, submit to the husbands, as it is fitting in [the] Lord.
pieces: Wives, submit to your husbands; this is fitting for those who belong to the Lord.

L.18: Wives, submit to [your] husbands, as is fitting in [the] Lord.

R.18: Wives, submit to your husbands, as is right for those who belong to the Lord.

decisions.choice: the household rules: Paul speaks to each member of the household
decisions.reason: Writers of the time set out the duties of household members (Aristotle, Politics 1.3), usually addressed to the man at its head. Paul speaks directly to wives, children and slaves as people answerable to the Lord, and gives husbands, fathers and masters duties too (3:19, 3:21, 4:1).

decisions.choice: submit: place oneself under, by one's own choice
decisions.reason: ὑποτάσσεσθε is middle: an act of the wife's own will. It is a different verb from "obey", which Paul uses for children and slaves (3:20, 3:22). In Ephesians 5:21 the same verb is used of all believers toward one another.

decisions.choice: as is fitting in the Lord: the measure is life in the Lord
alternatives: as is fitting by social custom
decisions.reason: ἀνῆκεν means what is proper or due. "In the Lord" makes life with Christ the measure, which both grounds the instruction and sets its limits.

decisions.choice: for those who belong to the Lord
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "in the Lord" means here.

records.heading: Life in the household

records.source: οἱ ἄνδρες, ἀγαπᾶτε τὰς γυναῖκας καὶ μὴ πικραίνεσθε πρὸς αὐτάς.
records.gloss: The husbands, love the wives and do not be bitter toward them.
pieces: Husbands, love your wives and never turn harsh or bitter against them.

L.19: Husbands, love [your] wives and do not be bitter toward them.

R.19: Husbands, love your wives. Never be unkind or bitter toward them.

decisions.choice: love: self-giving love
decisions.reason: ἀγαπάω is the love God shows and asks of his people. It is not a usual word in household rules of the time; Ephesians 5:25 measures it by Christ's love for the church.

decisions.choice: be bitter: grow resentful, or treat harshly
decisions.reason: πικραίνω means to make or become bitter. Husbands are not to let resentment turn into harsh treatment.

records.source: Τὰ τέκνα, ὑπακούετε τοῖς γονεῦσιν κατὰ πάντα, τοῦτο γὰρ εὐάρεστόν ἐστιν ἐν κυρίῳ.
records.gloss: The children, obey the parents in all things, this for pleasing is in [the] Lord.
pieces: Children, do what your parents tell you in everything, for that is what is pleasing in the Lord.

L.20: Children, obey [your] parents in all things, for this is pleasing in [the] Lord.

R.20: Children, always obey your parents. This is what the Lord wants.

decisions.choice: children: present when the letter was read
decisions.reason: The letter was read aloud to the gathered church (4:16), so children heard themselves addressed as members of it.

decisions.choice: in all things: a general rule, within life in the Lord
decisions.reason: κατὰ πάντα states the rule broadly; Ephesians 6:1 puts it "in the Lord", and verse 21 sets limits on the parents' side.

decisions.choice: pleasing in the Lord: what pleases the Lord among his people
decisions.reason: ἐν κυρίῳ may mean "to the Lord" or "among those in the Lord"; either way the Lord's pleasure is the reason.

decisions.choice: This is what the Lord wants
alternatives: this is pleasing in the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable puts the reason simply.

records.source: οἱ πατέρες, μὴ ἐρεθίζετε τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν, ἵνα μὴ ἀθυμῶσιν.
records.gloss: The fathers, do not provoke the children of you, so that not they lose heart.
pieces: Fathers, do not keep provoking your children, or they will lose heart.

L.21: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they do not lose heart.

R.21: Fathers, do not keep making your children angry, or they will give up trying.

decisions.choice: fathers
decisions.reason: πατέρες usually means fathers, though it can mean parents (Hebrews 11:23). Fathers held the authority in the household, which is why they are addressed.

decisions.choice: provoke ... lose heart: keep stirring them up until they give up
decisions.reason: ἐρεθίζω means to irritate or stir up; the present means doing it again and again. ἀθυμέω is to lose heart, to become discouraged.

records.source: οἱ δοῦλοι, ὑπακούετε κατὰ πάντα τοῖς κατὰ σάρκα κυρίοις, μὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοδουλίαις, ὡς ἀνθρωπάρεσκοι, ἀλλ’ ἐν ἁπλότητι καρδίας, φοβούμενοι τὸν κύριον.
records.gloss: The slaves, obey in all things the according to flesh masters, not with eye-service as people-pleasers, but in sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord.
pieces: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything. Do not work only while they are watching, to win their favor, but with an undivided heart, out of reverence for the Lord.

L.22: Slaves, obey in all things [your] masters according to the flesh, not with eye-service, as {{gender:people-pleasers|men-pleasers}}, but with sincerity of heart, fearing the Lord.

R.22: Slaves, obey your masters here on earth in everything. Do not work hard only when they are watching you, just to make them like you. Work with an honest heart, because you respect the Lord.

decisions.choice: slaves in the Roman world
decisions.reason: Slaves made up a large part of many households. They were legally their owners' property, though many were later freed. Slaves and masters belonged to the same churches (4:1; 4:9, where Onesimus is named; Philemon 10-16). The letter does not discuss whether slavery should exist; it speaks to people inside it and puts slaves and masters under one Lord (3:11; 4:1).

decisions.choice: masters according to the flesh, and the Lord: earthly owners, and Christ, their real Lord
decisions.reason: The same word, κύριος, means both "master" and "Lord". Their owners are masters only κατὰ σάρκα ("according to the flesh"), in this life; the Lord they fear is Christ (verse 24).

decisions.choice: eye-service: working only when watched, to please people
decisions.reason: ὀφθαλμοδουλίαις is first found in Paul's letters (also Ephesians 6:6): service done for the master's eye. ἀνθρωπάρεσκοι are those who aim only to please people.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "fearing the Lord"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "God". "The Lord" fits verses 23-24.

decisions.choice: masters (the owners); the Lord (Christ)
decisions.reason: One Greek word, two English ones (m2): "masters" for the owners and "Lord" for Christ, so that the contrast shows.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people-pleasers|men-pleasers}}
decisions.reason: The word means pleasing human beings; "men-pleasers" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: out of reverence for
decisions.reason: The fear meant is reverence (Proverbs 1:7); Literal keeps "fearing".

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level: Paul speaks to slaves as a social class, people actually owned, next to their "masters", and "servant" would change the meaning for modern readers (style guide); m1 says who they were.

records.source: ὃ ἐὰν ποιῆτε, ἐκ ψυχῆς ἐργάζεσθε, ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις, εἰδότες ὅτι ἀπὸ κυρίου ἀπολήμψεσθε τὴν ἀνταπόδοσιν τῆς κληρονομίας· τῷ κυρίῳ Χριστῷ δουλεύετε·
records.gloss: Whatever you do, from [the] soul work, as to the Lord and not to men, \v 24 knowing that from [the] Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; the Lord Christ you serve [as slaves];
pieces: Whatever you are doing, put your whole self into the work, as for the Lord and not for people,
knowing that you will receive from the Lord the inheritance as your reward. It is the Lord {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} you serve as slaves.

L.23: Whatever you do, work [at it] from the soul, as to the Lord and not to {{gender:people|men}},
L.24: knowing that from [the] Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; you are serving the Lord {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} as slaves.

R.23: Whatever work you do, give it everything you have, as if you were working for the Lord and not for people.
R.24: You know that the Lord will give you a reward: you will receive what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. You are really slaves of the Lord {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one you are serving.

decisions.choice: from the soul: wholeheartedly
decisions.reason: "From the soul" means with one's whole self (Ephesians 6:6).

decisions.choice: the reward of the inheritance: what slaves could not have, the Lord gives
decisions.reason: In law a slave could own nothing and inherit nothing. Yet the Lord will give these slaves the inheritance of his people (1:12) as their reward.

decisions.choice: you serve the Lord Christ: a statement of fact
alternatives: a command: serve the Lord Christ
decisions.reason: δουλεύετε can be a statement or a command. Many manuscripts add "for", which makes it a statement and the reason for verse 23. The verb is the one for serving as a slave: their true master is Christ.

decisions.choice: the Lord {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. "The Lord Messiah" is used without "the" before Messiah, since the phrase is a title.

decisions.choice: serve as slaves (L, B); slaves of the Lord Christ (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to serve as a slave. "Slave" is kept at every level: Paul speaks to slaves as a social class, people actually owned, next to their "masters", and "servant" would change the meaning for modern readers (style guide), and the verse tells them their true master is Christ (m3).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general; Balanced and Readable say "people".

decisions.choice: what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people
decisions.reason: Readable explains "inheritance" (m2 and 1:12).

records.source: ὁ γὰρ ἀδικῶν κομίσεται ὃ ἠδίκησεν, καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολημψία.
records.gloss: The [one] for doing wrong will receive back what he did wrong, and there is not partiality.
pieces: Anyone who does wrong will be repaid for that wrong, and there is no favoritism with the Lord.

L.25: For whoever does wrong will be repaid for the wrong done, and there is no partiality.

R.25: Whoever does wrong will be paid back for it. The Lord treats everyone the same.

decisions.choice: whoever does wrong: anyone, slave or master
alternatives: a master who wrongs his slaves
a slave who cheats his master
decisions.reason: The verse follows the words to slaves, but the next verse (4:1) turns to masters, and Ephesians 6:8-9 applies the same rule to both. No one's status changes how the Lord judges.

decisions.choice: partiality: favoring someone because of who they are
decisions.reason: προσωπολημψία comes from a Hebrew idiom, "to lift the face", meaning to favor a person (Deuteronomy 10:17; Romans 2:11). God does not judge by rank.

decisions.choice: with the Lord; The Lord treats everyone the same
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose impartiality is meant (verse 24; Ephesians 6:9).
